chapter: Harry Parker's, the district and its characters
title: Tough women: Mary Jack the Bear and Ann Cook
summary: Dawson says Mary Jack the Bear and Ann Cook were violent, recalls John Segretta's ballroom where Armstrong and Shots Madison played, and says he never knew Ann Cook as a singer.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: I know they had some bad women too back, I think too, you know. Mary Jack the Bear.
Well, she killed Black Benny, didn't she? She's the one who killed Black Benny. Yeah.
Thought she was tough, huh? Was she? They had some tough women too, Ron. What did she do?
Hustlin'. Did they, those women fight with their hands, Rebel? Yeah. Fight just like a man.

Pissed on? Yeah, that's a deed. Then fight with, both ways, with a razor and like, they all had big knives and razor. That's a deed. You getting the best of them, said you grab and take a razor out and slice you up with it. What about Ann Cook, was she? Ann Cook was nervous too. Yeah, she was tough. Mary Jack the Bear and Ann Cook, both of them was. Yeah. Yeah, they were really those.
We don't know too much about Ann Cook. Do you know what, did you know Ann Cook?

Ann Cook, I know Ann Cook when I was running up there around, uh, uh, uh, Segretta, John Segretta, you know John Segretta had a ballroom at the corner of Franklin and, uh, Grab here. Well, she lived around there? And she lived right around the corner of Franklin and, uh, they all bum-dancing. So, Greta had a ballroom and that's where, uh, Lewis Armstrong and, uh, and this fellow called Shutz, trumpet player. Uh, what's his first name now? Lewis Madison. Matt, Matt, Madison. Yeah, Lewis Madison. They called him Shutz for a nickname. He was a good trumpet player. Well, they all come from around that neighborhood. But did Ann Cook sing for a living ever? Uh, she could, but no, she hadn't, as I know her. She didn't sing without your band? No, no, as I know her, no.

Did you know Genevieve Davis? She played piano and sang. She recorded the same day that Ann Cook did. Where'd she recorded from? She, well, she from here, she recorded with Louis Dumaine. You see they had Louis Dumaine's band. Louis Dumaine, yeah, Louis Dumaine, uh, uh. Yeah, and Ann Cook and, and Genevieve Davis sang with the band. You mean you never saw Ann Cook singing in the band? No.
At least, uh, I don't remember, no. Did you ever hear her sing? No. You didn't even know what she sang? No.

But they had some tough guys around Jackson Avenue, too. I can't remember those brothers' names. But they were back around Jackson and, uh. White, wasn't it? I don't know. Jackson and Gravia, or, I mean, Jackson and Galvez, might be. I can't.
